newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan party chiefs say did not discuss poll timing.
newsitem.headline: Japan party chiefs say did not discuss poll timing.

text.p: The leaders of the three parties in Japan's ruling coalition did not discuss the timing of a general election at their meeting on Thursday, two of the leaders told reporters.
After meeting Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto, Social Democratic Party leader Tomiichi Murayama said there had been no mention of a general election at their meeting.
Hashimoto is also president of the Liberal Democratic Party, the largest party in the coalition.
"We discussed the issue of Okinawa only. There was no discussion on any possibility of a dissolution of parliament or general elections," Murayama said.
Shoichi Ide, head of New Party Sakigake, which is the other coalition partner, said Hashimoto would consult him and Murayama on the timing of any election whenever he was ready.
On Wednesday, Murayama and Ide expressed anger at a flurry of newspaper reports attributed to LDP sources which said a general election was likely to be held on October 20.

Hashimoto has said he would set a date for the election after confirming that Japan's economy was in full recovery and after settling a dispute with the southern island of Okinawa over U.S. military bases there.
Hashimoto does not need to hold general elections until July 1997.
